**Company**
Qualcomm Technologies, Inc.
  
  
**Job Area**
Engineering Group, Engineering Group > Modem Software Engineering
  
  
**General Summary**
Qualcomm is a company of inventors that unlocked 5G — ushering in an age of rapid acceleration in connectivity and new possibilities that will transform industries, create jobs, and enrich lives. But this is just the beginning. It takes inventive minds with diverse skills, backgrounds, and cultures to transform 5G's potential into world-changing technologies and products. This is the Invention Age — and this is where you come in.
  
  
The MMODE team develops protocol software that enables intelligent system selection and mobility across terrestrial and satellite wireless networks. MMODE software determines how devices discover, select, acquire, and transition between available connectivity options while balancing user experience, network performance, power efficiency, and operator requirements. Engineers work on technologies including 5G NR, LTE, NTN, Multi-SIM, emergency services, and next-generation connectivity solutions, collaborating closely with systems, modem firmware, and test teams to deliver innovative wireless features.
  
  
As a Modem Software Engineer, you will design, develop, and optimize real-time embedded software for Qualcomm's modem subsystem (MPSS). You will work close to the metal — writing performant, resource-constrained C/C++ that runs on DSP and Arm cores across cellular protocol layers, device drivers, and RTOS-level components.
  
  
Beyond traditional embedded development, this role is explicitly
**AI-native**
. You are expected to leverage, build, and improve AI-assisted development workflows — using code-generation agents, LLM-based code review, automated test synthesis, log/crash triage assistants, and retrieval-augmented tooling over our codebase — to dramatically accelerate delivery, quality, and debugging in a highly complex firmware environment.
  
  
**Principal Duties And Responsibilities**

* Design, implement, and optimize real-time embedded modem software across protocol layers, drivers, and platform services, meeting strict latency, memory, and power constraints.
* Apply rigorous data-structure and algorithm design to build efficient, scalable firmware components.
* Own end-to-end feature delivery: requirements, architecture, implementation, unit/integration testing, on-target bring-up, and maintenance.
* Pioneer AI-native development practices within the team — integrate AI coding agents into daily workflows, establish agent rules and prompt patterns, and measurably reduce development and debug cycle time.
* Build and maintain AI-assisted tooling for code review, static analysis, test synthesis, and automated crash/log triage over the modem codebase.
* Debug and root-cause complex, multi-layer issues on target hardware, increasingly leveraging AI-assisted analysis of logs, traces, and RAM dumps.
* Collaborate cross-functionally with systems, hardware, test, and integration teams to deliver production-quality modem firmware.
* Contribute to code reviews, design reviews, and continuous improvement of engineering standards — including standards for the responsible and effective use of AI in the SDLC.
* Mentor peers on both embedded fundamentals and AI-native engineering techniques.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or related field.

 - You have strong product and design taste and a clear sense of what “good” looks like

 - You take ownership and are comfortable driving an entire part of a product

 - You manage your own time and priorities well

WHY YOU MIGHT BE EXCITED ABOUT THIS OPPORTUNITY 🙌

 - Ship real products that get real usage, from customer-facing features to internal tools

 - Work cross-functionally. Partner with product, design, ops, GTM, data, and CS

 - Use the latest tech. Build with the latest coding tools and infrastructure

 - Move fast. Ship quickly and get rapid feedback from real users and teammates





WHY YOU MIGHT NOT BE EXCITED ABOUT US 👎

**Job Summary**
The Forward Deployed Specialist is the builder on the ground for WWT's Physical AI engagements, from the first prototype through a pilot running in the customer's environment. Where the Solution Architect owns the design, this role makes it work on real cameras and sensors, in a real plant or substation or stadium, with real operators watching the output. Perception comes first in Physical AI. Everything downstream, from an alert to a digital twin to a robot, is only as good as the visual data it receives, and the engineer is the person who finds out on day one whether the cameras can actually see what the use case needs.
  
  
The specialist works primarily on enterprise vision AI platforms, the kind that cover data curation, labeling, training, deployment and monitoring in one tool, using their SDKs and APIs when the engagement needs custom work and their low-code interfaces when it does not. The job is to wire the platform into the customer's cameras, sensors and existing systems, get a model trained and deployed on the customer's data, build the alerting and reporting that operations teams will actually use, and hand the result off to production with documentation someone else can run from. As the team grows, the same seat extends into digital twin, simulation and robotics engagements.
  
  
This is a hands-on builder role for someone comfortable prototyping a working example of an idea generated days earlier and staying with it until it runs in production. The raw material is video, sensor data, edge hardware and the operational systems a facility already runs on.
  
  
**Job Responsibilities**

* Builds the working system for each engagement phase. Ingests footage, curates and labels data, trains and evaluates models on the platform, deploys inference to the edge or cloud, and iterates with the customer until the output is trusted.
* Works fluently in the platforms' SDKs, APIs and workflow tools. Knows when the no / low-code path is enough and when to drop to code. Contributes reusable connectors, scripts and workflow templates back to the team.
* Connects to the customer's existing camera estate over RTSP or ONVIF and through their video management system. Integrates detections and events with the systems operators already use.
* Builds the alert logic, dashboards and reports that turn model output into something a line supervisor or field operations lead acts on. Tunes thresholds with the people who receive the alerts.
* Packages and deploys models to NVIDIA Jetson, on-prem GPU servers or cloud endpoints, including containerization, ONNX or TensorRT conversion, monitoring and rollback.
* Spends extended time at customer facilities during prototype and pilot phases. Understands the floor, learns the process, and adjusts camera placement, zones and event definitions with the operations team.
* Owns the retraining loop during the pilot. Diagnoses errors, pulls hard examples back into the training set, and documents the retraining triggers the customer inherits.
* Delivers runbooks, architecture notes, deployment scripts and a monitoring setup so the customer or WWT managed services can operate the system independently.
* Runs the hands-on portion of platform evaluations with the Solution Architect and product leadership, standing up the trial, loading the test dataset, executing the scoring scenarios and recording what broke.
* Builds and maintains demo environments and reference builds in the ATC and AI Proving Ground that sales and delivery teams can reuse.
* Extends the same build pattern into digital twin, simulation and robotics engagements, including synthetic data, simulation environments and robot or AMR integration alongside partners.
